question: On an SGLang OpenAI-compatible server, what makes structured message.tool_calls appear, which parser names exist for Qwen-family and other models, and what does tool_choice do?

budget.stop_reason: Every question in scope was answered by one primary page (launch flag, parser names, tool_choice) or shown to be a local check rather than a web question (launch argv, served model family). Excluded from scope and moved to open_questions.

sources.version_scope: current-main, unversioned; not pinned to the SGLang build running at :8012
sources.claim_taken: The launch flag --tool-call-parser selects the parser used to interpret responses; the supported-parsers table lists qwen, qwen3_coder and the other families; Tool Choice Mode documents tool_choice='required' and specific-function choice, implemented with EBNF grammar, fully supported on the default xgrammar backend.

claims.evidence: Launch example: python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct --tool-call-parser qwen25 --host 0.0.0.0 --log-level warning  # qwen25

claims.claim: The flag defines the parser used to interpret responses.
claims.evidence: Verbatim: 'Note that `--tool-call-parser` defines the parser used to interpret responses.'

claims.claim: Documented parser table: qwen (Qwen series except Qwen3-Coder), qwen3_coder (Qwen3-Coder), plus deepseekv3/deepseekv31/deepseekv32, glm, gpt-oss, kimi_k2, llama3, llama4, mistral, pythonic, step3, apertus2509.
claims.evidence: 'Currently supported parsers' table rows, verbatim model column: qwen -> 'Qwen series (e.g. Qwen/Qwen3-Next-80B-A3B-Instruct, Qwen/Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B-Thinking) except Qwen3-Coder'; qwen3_coder -> 'Qwen3-Coder (e.g. Qwen/Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B-Instruct)'.

claims.claim: qwen25 appears in the page's examples (launch, POST /parse_function_call body, FunctionCallParser) but is not a row of the supported-parsers table.
claims.evidence: Example tokens: '--tool-call-parser qwen25'; native API body '"tool_call_parser": "qwen25"'; offline 'FunctionCallParser(tools=tools, tool_call_parser="qwen25")'. Table rows are qwen and qwen3_coder only.

claims.claim: tool_choice is supported and implemented using EBNF grammar.
claims.evidence: Verbatim: 'SGLang supports OpenAI's `tool_choice` parameter to control when and which tools the model should call. This feature is implemented using EBNF (Extended Backus-Naur Form) grammar to ensure reliable tool calling behavior.'

claims.claim: Supported tool_choice values are 'required' (forces at least one tool call) and {type:function, function:{name:...}} (forces a specific function).
claims.evidence: Verbatim bullets: 'Forces the model to call at least one tool'; 'Forces the model to call a specific function'.

claims.claim: tool_choice is fully supported on the Xgrammar backend (the default, --grammar-backend xgrammar) and may not be fully supported on others such as outlines.
claims.evidence: Verbatim: 'Tool choice is fully supported with the Xgrammar backend, which is the default grammar backend (`--grammar-backend xgrammar`). However, it may not be fully supported with other backends such as `outlines`.'

claims.claim: The native endpoint POST /parse_function_call takes a per-request tool_call_parser and returns normal_text plus calls[].
claims.evidence: Example body {text, tool_call_parser: qwen25, tools} and response fields normal_text, calls[0].name, calls[0].parameters.

claims.claim: Without a tool parser configured, the OpenAI-compatible response carries no structured message.tool_calls.
claims.evidence: Reasoned from V1+V2 (the flag is what interprets responses, set in every tool example); the page never states the negative case. Owns a local check of the :8012 launch argv.

claims.claim: tool_choice is only meaningful where a tool parser is active; the documented dependency of tool_choice is the grammar backend, not the flag.
claims.evidence: V7 names the grammar backend as the dependency and the page never states 'tool_choice requires --tool-call-parser'. The plumbing-level requirement is inference.

claims.claim: A parser name that does not match the model family degrades to unparsed text rather than failing at startup.
claims.evidence: V3 pairs each parser with model families and qwen explicitly excludes Qwen3-Coder; the page documents no error behaviour for a mismatch. Makes the local family check load-bearing.

claims.claim: An SGLang server given tools returns structured tool_calls.
claims.evidence: Documented behaviour (V1, V4) vs our stack: 0 structured calls in 36 live requests (batch record, not re-measured by this card). Recorded as a disagreement, not resolved by citation: unresolved premises are (A) whether :8012 was launched with --tool-call-parser and (B) whether the parser name matches the served model family, both local checks.

changes_plan: The root-cause card becomes two local reads (launch argv for --tool-call-parser/--grammar-backend; served model id and family) before any further live tool-call battery.
No further live measurement is justified to establish documented behaviour; a live request is justified only to test premise A or B on this stack.
Any experiment varying tool_choice must also record --grammar-backend, because V7 makes the grammar backend the documented dependency.
A text-protocol shim, if adopted, is recorded as workaround:true and does not satisfy the tool-channel acceptance criterion.
open_questions: Q1 (local, owned by the root-cause card): was the :8012 server launched with --tool-call-parser, and with which name?
Q2 (local, owned by the root-cause card): which model family does occamy-1.0 belong to, i.e. which row of the parser table applies? Not speculated here.

Q3 (local): which SGLang build does :8012 run? The cited page is unversioned current-main docs, so version drift keeps claims about our build inferred until the package version or --help output is read.
Q4 (web, not fetched): are qwen25 and qwen the same parser, and does a mismatched parser fail loudly? The page is silent; the library source would answer it.
does_not_settle: Nothing about the :8012 server's configuration, version, or model family; nothing about whether any specific request on our stack will produce structured calls. Those are measurement and local-inspection questions, not documentation questions.
